translations.text: Because they could no longer hide him, his mother got a basket for him, coated it with pitch, put the little boy in it, and placed it among the reeds beside the river.
His sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Would you like me to call a nursing woman from among the Hebrews to nurse the little boy for you?”
The next day he went out and saw two Hebrew men fighting with each other. He said to the one who was doing wrong, “Why are you hitting your neighbor?”
Moses stayed with the man, and the man gave Moses his daughter Zipporah as his wife.
Moses said to God, “Who am I to go to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and bring the people out of the land of Egypt?”
The Lord said to Moses, “As you go back to Egypt, be sure to perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have put in your hands. But I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.”
Zipporah took a stone and circumcised her son’s foreskin. She fell at his feet and said, “The blood from my son’s circumcision has stopped.”
“You must no longer give the people straw for making bricks as you did before. Today let them go and gather straw for themselves.”
The taskmasters kept pressuring them, saying, “Complete the work assigned to you each day, just as you did when you were given straw.”
“I also established my covenant with them to give them the land of the Canaanites, the land where they lived as foreigners.”
“Go in and speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, so that he will let the children of [?] leave his land.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and instructed them to go to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to bring the children of [?] out of the land of Egypt.
The sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
“But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.”

“If Pharaoh speaks to you and says, ‘Give us a sign or a wonder,’ you must say to your brother Aaron, ‘Take the staff and throw it down on the ground before Pharaoh and his servants, and it will become a snake.’”
Each of them threw his staff down on the ground, and they became snakes. But Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs.
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs covered the whole land of Egypt.
Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord God.
“Look, the Lord’s hand will strike your livestock in the fields—the horses, the beasts of burden, the camels, the cattle, and the sheep—with a very great loss of life.”
“I will show my glory among the livestock of the Egyptians and among the livestock of the children of [?], so that none belonging to any of the children of [?] will die.”
“Look, at this time tomorrow I will rain down extremely heavy hail upon you, such as has never occurred in Egypt from the day it was founded until today.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, and hail will fall over the whole land of Egypt, on the people, the livestock, and every plant on the ground.”
Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said to them, “This time I have sinned. The Lord is righteous, but my people and I are wicked.”

Moses said to him, “Look, I will go outside the city and spread out my hands before the Lord. The thunder accompanying the hail will stop, and there will be no more rain, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the Lord.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and darkness and a storm came over the whole land of Egypt for three days.
For seven days no yeast is to be found in your houses. Anyone who eats anything leavened will be cut off from the congregation of [?], whether a foreigner or a native of the land.
And when your children say to you, “What is this ceremony?”
Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron during the night and said to them, “Get up and leave my people, both you and the children of [?]. Go and worship your God, as you have said.
Take your sheep and your cattle and go. And bless me too.”
No foreign resident or hired worker may eat any of it.
On that day the Lord brought the children of [?] out of the land of Egypt, along with their entire company.
The Lord said to Moses:
Pharaoh harnessed all his chariots and gathered all his people together with him.
Look, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, so that they go in after them. I will gain glory through Pharaoh and his entire army, and through his chariots and his horses.
The nations heard and trembled; pains seized those who live in Philistia.
Moses cried out to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he established ordinances and laws for him, and there he tested him.
Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of the children of [?], ‘Come forward into the presence of the Lord, for he has heard your grumbling.’”
They gathered it in the morning, each person the amount allotted to him. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
Moses said to them, “Eat it today, for today is the Lord’s Sabbath. You will not find any in the field.”
Jethro took burnt offerings and sacrifices to offer them to God. Aaron and all the elders of [?] came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.
Let them bring the important matter to you, but let them judge the minor cases themselves. They will give you relief and share the burden with you.
He chose capable men from all of [?] and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
In the third month after the children of [?] had come out of the land of Egypt, on that very day they came to the wilderness of Sin.
Let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down onto Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
The Lord spoke all these words, saying:
Honor your father and your mother, so that things may go well with you and you may live a long time on the good land that the Lord your God will give you.
If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must serve you for six years. In the seventh year he must go free without payment.
If he agrees to give her to his son, he must treat her according to the ordinance concerning daughters.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death.
If someone strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and the slave dies under his hands, he must certainly be punished.
But if it has taken form, he must give a life for a life.
If a fire breaks out and catches in thorns and burns threshing floors, standing grain, or a field, the person who lit the fire must replace what was burned.
If someone gives his neighbor a donkey, a calf, a sheep, or any animal to look after, and it dies or is carried off without anyone knowing,
You must observe everything I have told you. You must not mention the name of any other, foreign god, nor let their names be heard from your mouths.
You must bring the firstfruits of the earliest produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
They must not live with you in your land, so that they do not make you sin against me. For if you serve their gods, these will become a snare for you.
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it over the people. He said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has established with you concerning all these words.”
You must observe my Sabbaths, for the Sabbath is holy to the Lord and to you. Whoever profanes it must be put to death. Whoever does work on it, that person must be cut off from among his people.
All the people removed the gold earrings that were in the ears of their wives and daughters and brought them to Aaron.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying, “Leave this place quickly and go down, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.”
Moses pleaded before the Lord God, saying, “Why, Lord, are you angry with your people in your wrath, those whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your uplifted arm?”
The Lord said to him, “Here is a place beside me. You must stand on the rock.”
You must celebrate the Festival of Weeks for me, the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the beginning of the ingathering in the middle of the year.
You must place the first produce of your land in the house of the Lord your God. You must not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
